newsitem.title: LATVIA: New Latvian govt plans CPI fall, fiscal caution.
newsitem.headline: New Latvian govt plans CPI fall, fiscal caution.

text.p: The new government of Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele is working on a programme that includes planned inflation in 1997 of 11 percent, falling to nine percent in 1998, a draft of the programme showed on Tuesday.
Shkele was recalled to the premier's post last week after a shock resignation in mid-January.
He is now working on a new government programme that will be discussed with the parties that will form the government.
The draft programme said the new government would aim to fufill the planned balanced 1997 budget and reach five percent GDP growth per year.
As well as the inflation aims, the programme also foresees the proposal in September of a budget drawn up for two years and the launch on May 1 of two-year government T-bills.
The programme also says local government debt will only be allowed to rise to finance investment projects that will be profitable.
Shkele's first government was formed at the end of 1995 and he then set himself the aim of helping Latvia to recover from a damaging bank crisis in mid-1995.
The planned balanced budget came after a 35 million lat deficit in 1996 and a 90 million lat funding gap in 1995.
